labels.label: def:continuous_map_ordinary_locus
findings: Read literally, a set with empty preimage is evenly covered (vacuously), so every point outside the closure of p(X) is ordinary (GX.compl_closure_range_subset_ordY). This is what makes the two claims 'ord(Y) = ∅' at l.872 and l.880 false.
questions: Is the vacuous case intended (U with p^{-1}(U) = ∅ evenly covered)? The formalization follows the text. If not, the definition should add p^{-1}(U) ≠ ∅ or restrict to y ∈ closure p(X).

labels.label: rem:ordinary_locii_open_but

hypotheses.note: as LocallyConnectedSpace X, for the covering assertion only; openness needs nothing (ord(X) open needs p continuous)

findings: l.844: with mathlib's notion of covering map (fibres may be empty, total space need not be connected), ord(X) → ord(Y) is a covering whenever X is locally connected, connected or not (GX.isCoveringMap_restrict_ordX). If 'covering' includes surjectivity, connectedness of ord(X) is NOT the only obstruction: for the spread Unit → Bool, () ↦ true, ord(X) = Unit is connected and ord(Y) = Bool, but the restriction misses false (GX.unitTrue_counterexample), again because of the vacuous evenly-covered sets. It does hold for a surjective p (GX.surjective_restrict_ordX).
questions: What does 'covering' mean in the paper (surjective? connected total space?) — rem:ordinary_part_branched_covering (l.1001) suggests connected total space is part of it.

labels.label: cex:openess
findings: l.872: 'ord(Y) = ∅' is false as written: ord(Y) = ℝ² ∖ (ℝ×{0}) (GX.ordY_lineIncl), because a disc missing the line has empty preimage. What is true, and what the counterexample needs: Y₁ ∩ ord(Y) = ∅ and ord(X) = ∅ (GX.cex_openess). Suggested wording: 'but ord(X) = ∅ and ord(Y) ∩ Y₁ = ∅'.

labels.label: cex:portlyness

hypotheses.note: for 'p(x) ∉ ord(Y)'; the non-injectivity itself needs only p continuous, Y₁ open and the restriction an open map

findings: Item 1 holds and is proved as a theorem (GX.notMem_ordX_of_notMem_interior).

Item 2, l.880: 'ord(Y) = ∅' is false as written: p(X) avoids the open unit disc (‖p(x)‖ ≥ 1), so the disc is (vacuously) ordinary whatever topology X carries (GX.ball_subset_ordY_portlyInv). The intended claim is ord(Y) ∩ p(X) = ∅.

Item 2's own space (X ⊆ ℝ² with 'the coarsest topology making the injection a spread') is not built. A counterexample with every property the paper lists (X = ℝ connected, Hausdorff, second countable, locally path-connected; p = x ↦ ||x|-1| a spread; X₁ = (1,∞) open and locally connected in X but not dense; Y₁ = (0,∞) open; X₁ → Y₁ a homeomorphism) is GX.cex_portlyness: 1 ∉ ord(Y), 2 ∈ X₁ ∖ ord(X), and p^{-1}(Y₁) ∋ -2 so p^{-1}(Y₁) ≠ X₁.
questions: l.877: 'the coarsest topology making the natural injection X → Y a spread' — such a coarsest topology is not obviously well defined (spreadness depends on components, which depend on the topology). Which topology is meant: the one generated by the subspace-topology components of X ∩ U?

hypotheses.note: any maps; only g, f homeomorphisms with p₂ ∘ g = f ∘ p₁ are used

kb_proposals: The paper's 'evenly covered' is vacuous on sets with empty preimage, so ord(Y) ⊇ Y ∖ closure p(X); any 'ord(·) = ∅' claim must be checked against it.

From an evenly covered set to mathlib's IsEvenlyCovered: IsOpen.trivializationDiscrete with ι = the set of components (⊥ topology), then IsEvenlyCovered.of_trivialization and .to_isEvenlyCovered_preimage; empty preimage via of_preimage_eq_empty (GX.isEvenlyCovered_of_isEvenlyCoveredSet).
A homeomorphism is a covering map via IsClosedMap.isCoveringMapOn_of_openPartialHomeomorph (needs T2 source); mathlib has no Homeomorph.isCoveringMap at fabf563a.
Cheap spreads on ℝ: a map with |f z - f x| = |z - x| locally (GX.IsLocDistPres) is a spread; compositions of abs and translations give folds.
